reviewer: repo owner (szablevi@gmail.com), in-session review with the coding agent
purpose: Manual spot-check of a random sample of translated artefacts against their original source material, as human evidence supplementing the automated QA suite (issue #103) before issue #106 is closed.
artefact_definition: Every individually source-mapped element in translation.json's `mappings` list: classes, class properties, relationships, rules, actions (175 total). Competency questions were excluded from the artefact population -- they are synthesized from the whole domain rather than mapped from specific source IRIs, so there is no 'original source info' to check them against in the same way.

sampling_method.description: Stratified sample by artefact type, proportional allocation with largest-remainder rounding, fixed random seed for reproducibility.

items.reviewer_comment: check the original ontology docs if this is allowed
items.finding: rec:status in the pinned Brick source (Brick.ttl) is a bare owl:DatatypeProperty with only an rdfs:label -- no comment, no range, no enumeration. There is no source-doc basis for any specific allowed-value set on 'status'. Separately, and independent of source grounding: agent_ontology_spec.md Section 5 types `allowed` as `string[] | null`. This class's allowed list was [false, true, 'cooling', 'alarm'] -- YAML booleans mixed with strings, a direct type violation of our own format spec, not just a grounding weakness. The same defect was found on 15 other classes' status.allowed list via a full scan (16 total): AHU, Boiler, Chiller, Compressor, CondensingUnit, CoolingTower, Fan, HeatExchanger, Humidifier, Pump, SpaceHeater, TerminalUnit, Thermostat, WallAirConditioner, CRAC, CRAH.

code_fix: ontology_translation/tools/validate_domain.py: structural gate now flags allowed_not_all_strings when any entry in a property's `allowed` list is not a str (agent_ontology_spec.md types `allowed` as `string[] | null`) -- previously only checked that `allowed` was a list at all.
ontology_translation/tools/tests/test_validate_domain.py: added coverage for the new check.

ontology_translation/tools/prompts/compiler-prompt.md: added an explicit instruction that `allowed` entries must always be plain strings, never bare YAML booleans, with the Brick CRAH finding cited as the reason.
remediation.data_fix: Manually edited domains/brick-hvac/reference.domain.yaml: replaced the literal YAML values `false`/`true` with the strings "off"/"on" in the `status.allowed` list of all 16 affected classes (AHU, Boiler, Chiller, Compressor, CondensingUnit, CoolingTower, Fan, HeatExchanger, Humidifier, Pump, SpaceHeater, TerminalUnit, Thermostat, WallAirConditioner, CRAC, CRAH). No other content changed -- diff is exactly these 32 lines. This was a manual correction, NOT a fresh LLM compile/re-run: the underlying compiler was not re-invoked, no Azure API calls were made for this fix, and the rest of the translation's content and provenance rationale are unchanged from the originally accepted candidate.
remediation.re_validation: Re-ran the (free, offline, deterministic) structural gate -- tools/validate_domain.py domains/brick-hvac/reference.domain.yaml -- against the corrected file with the new allowed_not_all_strings check active: 0 errors, 0 warnings. Full offline test suite (95 tests) also re-run and passing.
remediation.not_done: No LLM compile or evaluate re-run was performed as part of this fix, per explicit instruction. translation-evaluation.json's semantic-judging, round-trip and CQ-support numbers are unchanged from the original accepted run and reflect the pre-fix content for those layers (none of which touched the `allowed` lists).
